user.title: Set up HCL Lighting
user.description: Configure the Human Centric Lighting integration. The wake and sleep time create the default curve; it can be edited later in the dashboard card.

error.active_span_too_short: Wake and sleep time must be more than 6 hours apart.
error.no_lights: Select at least one light, area, device, floor or label.

init.title: HCL Lighting options
init.description: A curve saved in the dashboard card has priority over the anchor times. Changing the wake or sleep time discards it and creates a new default curve.

data.override_timeout: Return to HCL after manual control (min, 0 = never)
data.override_reset_on_off: Switching a light off ends manual control
data.respect_turn_on_values: Keep values of turn-on commands (scenes, automations, voice)

data_description.respect_turn_on_values: If a light is switched on through Home Assistant with its own brightness or colour, HCL leaves it as it is (manual control).

data_description.update_interval: Seconds between two update cycles (15–300, default 27).
data_description.transition: Seconds; must be shorter than the update interval (default 20). Lights without transition support ignore it.
data_description.scenario_transition: Seconds (default: same as the update transition). Also used when a scenario ends and returns to Auto; may be longer than the update interval.

scenarios.title: Scenarios
scenarios.description: Focus, Relax and Cleaning stay within the minimum and maximum brightness. Sleep and Night light end at the next wake time.

daylight.title: Daylight compensation
daylight.description: Optional: an indoor lux sensor lowers the brightness in Auto when there is enough daylight. The brightness never goes above the curve and never below the minimum brightness; the colour temperature is not changed. Choose a sensor that represents the room and is not lit directly by the lights.

data_description.daylight_sensor: Sensor with device class illuminance (lx), required when the daylight compensation is on.
data_description.daylight_target_lux: Lux at the sensor HCL aims for (50–2000, required when on). A control value at the sensor position, not a lighting standard value.

data.daylight_unavailable_grace: Grace for a missing sensor value

data_description.daylight_deadband_lux: Lux around the target without a change (empty: 5 % of the target, at least 20 lx).
data_description.daylight_smoothing: Time constant of the lux filter in seconds (default 60).
data_description.daylight_response_band_lux: Lux deviation that uses the full rate (default 300); smaller deviations change the brightness more slowly.
data_description.daylight_max_rate: Percent points per minute (default 11), independent of the update interval.
data_description.daylight_stale_after: Seconds without a report until the value counts as outdated (default 3600; 0 = no check, for sensors that report only on change).
data_description.daylight_unavailable_grace: Seconds the reduction is held while the sensor has no valid value (default 300); afterwards the brightness returns slowly to the curve.

error.min_greater_max: Minimum brightness must be lower than maximum.
error.transition_too_long: The transition must be shorter than the update interval.
error.active_span_too_short: Wake and sleep time must be more than 6 hours apart.
error.no_lights: Select at least one light, area, device, floor or label.
error.daylight_sensor_required: Choose a lux sensor for the daylight compensation.
error.daylight_target_required: Enter the target illuminance for the daylight compensation.

update_curve.name: Update curve
update_curve.description: Update the HCL control points (used by the dashboard card).

entity_id.name: Entity
entity_id.description: The HCL switch or curve sensor.

points.name: Control points
points.description: Control points with t (0-1440 min), b (0-100 %) and k (2000-7000 K), at least 2, each time only once. Not used for revert.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: preview/apply: use the points until the next reload; save: store them; revert: reload the saved curve.

apply.name: Apply HCL values
apply.description: Sends the current HCL values to lights that are on right away. Never switches lights on; lights under manual control are skipped.

entity_id.name: HCL instance
entity_id.description: Any entity of the HCL instance (switch, scenario or sensor).

lights.name: Lights
lights.description: Lights of the instance; empty = all.

release_manual_control.name: Release manual control
release_manual_control.description: Also hand lights under manual control back to HCL.

set_manual_control.name: Set manual control
set_manual_control.description: Pauses HCL for lights (on) or hands them back to HCL (off).

entity_id.name: HCL instance
entity_id.description: Any entity of the HCL instance (switch, scenario or sensor).

lights.name: Lights
lights.description: Lights of the instance; empty = all.

manual_control.name: Manual control
manual_control.description: On: HCL pauses the lights; off: they follow HCL again.

set_scenario.name: Set scenario
set_scenario.description: Selects a scenario, optionally for a duration.

entity_id.name: HCL instance
entity_id.description: Any entity of the HCL instance (switch, scenario or sensor).

scenario.name: Scenario
scenario.description: auto, sleep, night_light, focus, relax, cleaning or guest (deprecated, removed in 0.9.0).

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Minutes until the return to Auto (0 = until changed). Empty: Focus/Relax/Cleaning use the configured duration, Sleep/Night light end at the next wake time.

get_curve.name: Get curve
get_curve.description: Returns the points of the active and the saved curve and the wake and sleep time (e.g. to copy them to another instance with update_curve).

entity_id.name: HCL instance
entity_id.description: Any entity of the HCL instance (switch, scenario or sensor).

light_in_multiple_instances.title: Light in several HCL instances
light_in_multiple_instances.description: {light} is controlled by several HCL instances ({instances}) that adapt the same attribute. They overwrite each other. Remove the light from one instance or turn off “Adapt brightness” or “Adapt colour temperature” there.

guest_deprecated.title: Scenario “Guest” of {instance} will be removed
guest_deprecated.description: The scenario Guest is deprecated and will be removed in version 0.9.0: it does the same as switching “HCL active” off. Switch “HCL active” off instead (also in automations with hcl_lighting.set_scenario) and select another scenario; this message disappears when {instance} leaves Guest.

daylight_shared_sensor.title: Lux sensor used by several HCL instances
daylight_shared_sensor.description: {sensor} is the lux sensor of the daylight compensation of several active HCL instances ({instances}). Two control loops on one sensor work against each other when their lights reach it. Use one sensor per lighting zone that represents it, or turn the daylight compensation off in all but one instance. Ignore this message if the instances light separate rooms that the sensor does not see.

guest_mode.message: HCL sends no values in Guest mode

not_controlled.message: Not controlled by this HCL instance: {lights}

not_hcl_entity.message: {entity_id} is not an HCL Lighting entity

instance_not_loaded.message: The HCL instance of {entity_id} is not loaded

scenario_unavailable.message: The scenario of this HCL instance is not available

lights_no_answer.message: No answer from {pending} within {seconds} s (command still running)
